title: 2027 BRIT Awards Trophy Designed by ‘One of Britain’s Greatest Living Artists’: See Photos
summary: The trophy will be presented to winners at the ceremony on Feb. 27 in Manchester.
body: The 2027 BRIT Awards trophy has been designed by former Turner Prize-winning visual artist Dame Rachel Whiteread (Nov. 27). Each year a different designer shapes a distinct creative vision for their trophy, modeled on the image of Britannia, traditionally represented by a female warrior with a shield and helmet. In recent years, the trophy has been designed by iconic names such as Dame Vivienne Westwood, Sir Peter Blake, Tracey Emin, Dame Zaha Hadid, and last year’s designer, Matthew Williamson. Whiteread took on 2027’s assignment, and her trophy will be presented to winners at the ceremony on Feb. 27 at the Co-op Live in Manchester. In 1993, Whiteread became the first woman to win the Turner Prize, an accolade presented annually to a British visual artist; previous victors include Damien Hirst, Gilbert & George, and Anish Kapoor. Four years after her win, in 1997, she was the first woman to represent Britain at the Venice Biennale. Her work primarily focuses on casting, and her Turner Prize-winning exhibit House (1993) featured a life-sized concrete cast of a Victorian terraced house in east London. body: Credit: TCL CSOT A screen has a big impact on how a device feels to use. title: New Play Store requirements force app developers to publish their addresses online
summary: The only way to avoid Google's requirement is to pull your apps from Europe and the UK.
body: Credit: Megan Ellis / Android Authority TL;DR Google is reportedly facing privacy concerns over a requirement for app developers to disclose their phone numbers and physical addresses. The requirement applies to all app developers, including solo creators, who offer their apps in Europe and the UK. The company won’t allow developers to use a PO box, leading at least one creator to say they might rent a separate office. Google and partners started rolling out developer verification for Android apps earlier this year, along with a more convoluted sideloading process on devices. These new measures will launch globally in January , but another Google requirement is under scrutiny due to privacy issues. The Elec reports that Google is facing privacy concerns over a recent requirement that app developers (including solo creators) publicly disclose their phone numbers and physical addresses on Google Play. This move, which kicks in from March 2027, is meant to help Google and developers comply with European regulatory requirements. However, the outlet adds that developer addresses and phone numbers will be shown worldwide.
